newsitem.title: USA: Aerospace seen fueling United Tech growth.
newsitem.headline: Aerospace seen fueling United Tech growth.

text.p: A soaring aerospace unit will keep United Technologies Corp. on a flight path towards strong earnings growth for the next few quarters, analysts said Wednesday.
The industrial-technology company is on target to meet or exceed 1997 earnings per share of $4.05, against 1996 earnings of $3.45, they said.
United Technologies on Wednesday posted a net of $304 million or $1.17 a share in the second quarter, slightly beating a First Call estimate of 15 analysts of $1.14 a share.
This compared with a $259 million net, or $0.98 a share, for the quarter last year.
United Technologies' stock was down 0-1/8 at 86-1/8 in late trading on Wednesday, on volume of 942,700 shares.
"Aerospace will continue to fuel the growth," said Michael Bunyaner, an analyst at Oppenheimer & Co.
"This is a long-term business where backlogs are such that you know what your volumes are going to be like, for at least a year or two out."

The company's jet-engine manufacturing unit, Pratt & Whitney, led the second-quarter growth, due to higher aftermarket sales and increased commercial and military engine shipments, United Technologies said.
"Pratt and the aerospace group are going to act like a very impressive horse (to drive future growth)," said Howard Rubel, analyst at Goldman Sachs.

Flight Systems' second-quarter operating profit grew by 11 percent on 9 percent higher revenues, due to double-digit revenue growth and improved margins at Hamilton Standard and continued strong performance at helicopter manufacturer Sikorsky Aircraft.
"Pratt has been at their cost-cutting efforts for close to four years," Bunyaner said. "They're clearly working, and they're now seeing the benefits of a very significant re-design of the business."
"In general, over the last four or five years this company really changed its focus from the size to the quality of its businesses, and the profitability," he said.
"You are seeing a great deal of benefit from a very signficant focus on costs, and also efficiencies."
Bunyaner noted that United Technologies' asset utilization has improved, and that cash flow is very strong.
"Not only are they focussing on how well they run their businesses, but they've also done a very good job of focussing on how much capital it takes to run those businesses."
The company's industrial businesses are doing very well, except for automotive, analysts said.
"Automotive will eventually get fixed," Rubel said. "They've fixed every other problem that appeared to be insurmountable."
Among United Technologies' other units, Otis is the world's biggest producer of elevators, and Carrier is the world's biggest producer of heating and air-conditioning systems.
